subject: business-studies
title: Stakeholders vs Shareholders
welcome_lead: Whose interests should the business serve - owners alone, or everyone affected?
meta_desc: A-Level External Environment: stakeholder mapping and shareholder primacy.
final_note: Stakeholder mapping turns conflicting demands into a clear set of priorities.

concepts.def: Owner of shares in a company entitled to profit and votes.
Anyone affected by or affecting the business.
Plotting stakeholders by power and interest.
Corporate Social Responsibility - voluntary ethical action.
Reporting on people, planet and profit, not just profit.
Conflict between managers' interests and shareholders'.

walkthroughs.body_html: Mendelow plots stakeholders on power and interest. High-power, high-interest groups must be managed closely; low-power, low-interest groups need only minimal effort.
The Friedman view holds that managers' duty is to maximise shareholder value within the law. Critics argue it ignores externalities and long-term value destruction.
The triple bottom line measures social, environmental and financial performance. Patagonia and Unilever push it; critics call it greenwashing when not backed by action.

options: Owner of preference shares
Local community near the factory
Holder of ordinary shares
Institutional investor

options: Power and Interest
Profit and Risk
Growth and Share
Cost and Quality

mcqs.q: How do stakeholder and shareholder interests overlap and conflict?
options: Shareholders are external and stakeholders are internal.

Shareholders are a subset of stakeholders. Their interests overlap (long-term success benefits all) but conflict on issues like dividends vs investment, wages vs profits, or short-term gains vs long-term sustainability.
Stakeholders and shareholders always want the same thing.
Stakeholders are managers and shareholders are workers.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between a stakeholder and a shareholder?
options: Shareholders are external and stakeholders are internal.
A shareholder owns shares in the company; a stakeholder is anyone affected by or with interest in the business — employees, customers, suppliers, community, plus shareholders.
Stakeholders and shareholders are different spellings of the same word.
Stakeholders are managers and shareholders are workers.
PESTLE stands for Profit, Earnings, Sales, Trade, Loans, Equity.
Shareholders are external and stakeholders are internal.
The external macro-environment: Political, Economic, Social, Technological, Legal and Environmental factors affecting a business.
PESTLE analyses the internal strengths and weaknesses of a business.
